WSL cache lesson from this batch: project `.lake/build` metadata is path
sensitive.  Seeding it from an older mirror caused Lake to invoke `/mnt/c`
source paths even after the source snapshot had been copied to ext4.  For a
fresh verification mirror, preserve only compatible package caches, recreate
the project `.lake/build`, and inspect Lean command paths before accepting a
build.  A copied dirty `.git` can also make Lake's `git diff HEAD --exit-code`
stdout block on a pipe; for verification-only commands, setting
`GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF=true` suppresses that diff payload without staging or
changing the mirror's Git state.  Always verify `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
and all Lean input/output paths before relying on the result.

therefore contains the RH-level arithmetic breakthrough. Treat ownership and
sign as separate gates.

## Lean Rules Worth Remembering

### Row-record destructuring

For an existential plus a conjunction whose final item is a structure, split
the outer pair before extracting the structure:

```lean
rcases h with ⟨r, hmatch⟩
have hr := hmatch.1
have rows := hmatch.2
```

A flat `rcases h with ⟨r, hr, rows⟩` can recursively destruct the final record.

### Type versus Prop

A data-bearing structure lives in `Type`. Use:

```text
P and Nonempty Rows
```

when only existence is needed, or use a Sigma/data structure when later code
must retain the witness. Do not write a `Type` record directly as a conjunct of
a proposition.

### Dependent owner transport

`owner.sameSymbols : routeSymbols = ownerSymbols` does not transport
certificate data that depends on the entire owner. Use a theorem that states
the required equality or `HEq` for every dependent component. Keep unproved
transport experiments outside compiled route APIs.

### Constructor names

When an inductive constructor has a mathematical name such as `rho`, use a
different local parameter name and write `.rho` at call sites.

### Import artifacts

Direct `lake env lean File.lean` can pass while imported `.olean` artifacts are
stale. Accepted verification requires an importing scratch file with `#check`
and `#print axioms`. If the import misses a new declaration after the smallest
build, remove only that module's stale artifacts and rebuild that target.

## 2026-07-11 Rejection-First Route Order

Do not continue xi-counting merely because its local bottom is available. The
highest-value next gate is the CC20 Corollary 3.8 (`qeasy`) factorization:

```text
selected Yoshida square = Q(f),
f positive definite,
support inside [u^-1,u], u = 1.10246.
```

CC20 Theorem 3.6 confirms that M3A's abstract `-2 Id + K_I` shape is genuine;
M3A is therefore primarily an ownership/normalization formalization risk, not
the most likely mathematical rejection. The more dangerous issue is whether
the same detector can satisfy the finite bad-space constraints while retaining
nonzero Mellin value at `rho`.

Test `qeasy` first because it can remove that issue entirely. The compiled
`convolutionIterate_rescale_inv_natCast_convolution_support_subset_half_budget`
shows that support width does not obstruct this subroute: an arbitrary outer
log window can be divided between the normalized base power and correction.
The unresolved rejection gate is algebraic positivity-preserving factorization,
not support. If factorization fails, immediately test joint separation of the
`rho` Mellin evaluation from the concrete M4 bad-space functionals. Reject the
fixed-window route if that joint separation is false; do not finish peripheral
counting or trace layers first.

## 2026-07-11 Plan 016 Rejection

The rejection-first audit rejects plan 016 as an executable RH route. The
assembled Yoshida theorem does not preserve correction interpolation:

```text
Phi_assembled(rho)
  = Phi_base(rho/(n+1))^(n+1) * Phi_correction(rho).
```

Thus `Phi_correction(rho)=1` does not imply detection; a zero base factor makes
the assembled value zero. The compiled rejection guard is
`laplaceAt_convolutionIterate_rescale_inv_natCast_convolution_eq_zero_of_base`.

The same assembly also has an unclosed radius/count cycle. The nearby radius
`R` is fixed before the correction constant and convolution count `n` exist,
while the far estimate begins only beyond `(n+1)*T`. No current bound or
fixed-point theorem proves that the original nearby set covers every zero below
that later threshold. Therefore finite nearby interpolation plus the current
far estimate does not yield one Appendix C detector.

The `qeasy` support budget is feasible but cannot repair the absent detector;
it supplies only the local remainder sign. M5B is rejected in its current form,
and M5C/M6/root retirement are inactive. Do not resume xi-counting, M2, or M3A
under plan 016. A future plan may reopen the broad strategy only after a new
non-circular producer proves full-product normalization and a simultaneous
all-zero tail bound on the same compact test.

## 2026-07-11 Plan 018 D1 Rejection

The Suzuki screw-norm defect has an unconditional absolutely convergent
one-dimensional integral formula, and finite symmetric zero truncations split
exactly into a `K_R-I` Gram term plus an off-critical conjugation term. The
source does not supply an absolutely convergent zero-pair expansion or a
summable pair majorant: local absolute convergence of `P_t` and global `L2`
membership of `S_t` do not justify termwise expansion of the norm. Gram
positivity controls `K_R`, not `K_R-I`, so it gives no defect sign. Plan 018 is
rejected at D1 as a guaranteed route; no Lean API or RH root changes result.

## 2026-07-11 Plan 019 H2/H3 Rejection

The proposed adelic Cech--Hodge regrading of the CC20 remainder fails at the
H2/H3 interface. In a scaling-equivariant Hilbert complex, legal exact and
coexact trace contributions pair and cancel, leaving no `K_I` remainder. The
support/Fourier cutoff product that actually generates the CC20 small square is
non-idempotent, has prolate eigenvalues in `(0,1)`, and does not commute with
full scaling. Moreover `-2 Id + K_I` has a positive direction on the larger
window and a negative infinite-dimensional tail, so it is not one signed
boundary norm. Splitting off its finite bad eigenspace is exactly the existing
finite-codimension conditioning, not a new producer. Plan 019 is rejected; no
Lean API or RH root changes result.

## 2026-07-11 Plan 020 Nyman--Mobius Dyadic Experiment

Plan 020 began as the rejection-first research entrypoint. It leaves the
Connes route and uses the exact discrete Nyman--Beurling--Baez-Duarte criterion
`RH <=> d_N -> 0` in the weighted sequence space with weights
`1/(n*(n+1))`. For each dyadic block it selects the explicit direction

```text
b_N = sum_(N<k<=2N) mu(k)/k * gamma_k.
```

Orthogonal projection gives an exact finite energy decrement. A uniform bound

```text
certificate_capture >= (c/log N) * d_N^2
```

would force `d_N -> 0` because the dyadic factors have a divergent harmonic
exponent. The bridge is valid and does not read zeta zeros. Its central lower
bound is unproved and must be obtained from finite residue/divisor sums rather
than Littlewood, Mertens square-root cancellation, or convergence of the
natural Mobius approximants.

The first WSL2 experiment is positive but non-rigorous. With tail cutoff two
million, the normalized `mu(k)/k` capture at `N=16,32,64,128` is approximately
`0.426, 0.578, 0.554, 0.616`. Results are stable across cutoffs from `250000`
to `2000000`; exact or interval inner products remain mandatory because the
Gram systems become increasingly ill-conditioned. See
`plan/020_2026-07-11_nyman_mobius_dyadic_certificate_plan.md` and
`scratch_nyman_block.py`.

Initial judgment: Plan 020 had passed the exact criterion, projection identity,
and dyadic closure gates, and has survived a first numerical rejection test.
It is not yet a guaranteed RH route. The next and most likely rejection gate is
M4: expand the Mobius block correlation and projected energy exactly and decide
whether divisor orthogonality supplies a strict `c/log N` margin without an
RH-equivalent cancellation estimate.

The first M4 audit did not reject the route. Exact periodic summation proves
`<gamma,gamma_k>=log(k)/k` and gives every Gram entry as a finite digamma sum
over one `lcm(j,k)` period. Exact and two-million-term results agree through
`N=32`. A larger cutoff experiment gives normalized `mu(k)/k` captures about
`0.4140` at `N=256` and `0.5802` at `N=512`, so no scale collapse is visible.

The audit also identified the actual analytic bottom. The correlation and
projected energy contain the inverse old Gram matrix `G_N^-1`; the elementary
Mobius divisor identity does not remove it. Baez-Duarte's direct natural
Mobius approximations are known to diverge in `L2` (arXiv:math/0011254,
Propositions 4.4--4.7), but that theorem does not cover Plan 020 because each
block is first projected by `(I-P_N)`. At that checkpoint Plan 020 remained
active but unresolved, not guaranteed. See
`docs/proofs/020_nyman_mobius_m4_first_verdict.md`.

The first structural M4 subroute is rejected. Vasyunin's finite-support
biorthogonal family satisfies `<gamma_m,f_n>=delta_(m,n)`, but it is the dual
of the infinite minimal system. The finite canonical dual is `P_N f_n`, which
reintroduces `G_N^-1`; at `N=64`, it retains only about 14.8 percent of the
squared norm of `f_64`. A Cholesky positivity conjecture found in
arXiv:2011.02847 is unproved and would not close the signed target-coordinate
sum even if true. Do not reopen this subroute.

One valid M4 reduction remains: with
`S_N=sum_(N<k<=2N) mu(k)/k^2`, the vector
`b_N-N*S_N*gamma_N` vanishes in the first `N-1` coordinates and
`w_N=(I-P_N)(b_N-N*S_N*gamma_N)`. Its values are explicit short weighted
Mobius floor sums. This localizes the denominator but not the numerator; the
projection still removes a material fraction of its energy. See the updated
020 verdict.

The source audit found unconditional power-saving upper bounds for related
Mobius--Vasyunin short sums in Maier--Rassias, arXiv:1705.09921, Theorem 1.1.
They may help the localized denominator but have the wrong inequality direction
for M4: the numerator needs a uniform inverse-Gram non-cancellation lower bound.
The active mathematical bottom is now named
`inverse-Gram Mobius non-cancellation`. Plan 020 remains unresolved rather than
rejected, while both the Vasyunin-direct-inverse and Cholesky-positivity
shortcuts are rejected.

The next M4 sign audit rejects pointwise positivity. The sequential
Gram--Schmidt target coordinate has the wrong sign relative to `-mu(n)` already
at the squarefree index `n=31`; exact periodic and two-million-term Gram
computations agree on the negative value. There are 24 squarefree sign failures
through `n=256`. Do not seek a proof that every Mobius-weighted future
correlation is nonnegative.

The certificate is robust to replacing `mu(k)/k` by `mu(k)/k^alpha` over the
broad range `-1<=alpha<=2`, so its numerical behavior is not fine exponent
tuning. The Bettin--Conrey--Farmer log taper is weaker in the block experiment,
and its published asymptotic assumes RH plus a moment bound on
`1/zeta'(rho)`. The remaining 020 numerator bottom is block-average Mobius
dominance with individual sign failures allowed.

A good/bad contribution audit shows that even fixed-fraction block dominance
is not a sound intermediate target. For `mu(k)/k`, the bad/good absolute mass
ratio grows from about `0.051` at `N=32` to `0.509` at `N=512`. M4 survives
numerically because the projected Schur energy shrinks concurrently. The only
admissible remaining bottom is therefore the coupled normalized inequality,
not separate coarse numerator and denominator bounds.

The final rejection-first round rejects Plan 020 as an executable RH route,
without claiming that M4 is mathematically false. A matrix-free CUDA projection
run extended the selected direction to `N=4096`. The normalized values
`log(N)*capture/d_N^2` at `N=1024,2048,4096` were approximately
`0.2948,0.5869,0.2664` at cutoff `250000`; cutoff `100000` gave `0.2965` and
`0.2834` at the two low scales. Both normal-equation residuals were below
`1e-11`. This replaces the earlier stable-margin impression with strong dyadic
oscillation and descending low subscales, but it is not a rigorous zero-infimum
certificate because the projected energy is below the crude tail-mass bound.

The route-level rejection is structural. Vasyunin duality, Cholesky positivity,
pointwise signs, fixed-fraction good/bad dominance, power weights, and the BCF
log taper all fail to lower M4. The surviving coupled inequality retains
`G_N^-1`, implies RH through the checked dyadic closure, and has no independent
unconditional arithmetic producer. Burnol supplies only the lower obstruction
on `d_N^2 log N`; the matching BCF Mobius asymptotic assumes RH plus a moment
bound on `1/zeta'(rho)`. Plan 020's exact formulas remain reusable evidence, but
do not reopen this route without a genuinely lower inverse-Gram theorem.

## 2026-07-11 Plan 021 Divisor-Gradient Flow Rejection

The self-derived divisor-gradient correction is rejected. The exact identity

```text
Delta gamma_k(n) = 1/k - 1_(k divides n)
```

allows unique coefficients in `N<k<=2N` that cancel every gradient of the old
optimal residual on `N<n<=2N`. CUDA checks confirm the local cancellation to
about `1e-16`. Globally, however, the same coefficients hit all later multiples
and increase weighted Hilbert energy. At `N=32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048`, the
raw energy ratios were approximately
`15.73,1.31,3.35,10.13,2.98,2.60,4.72`; after old-space reprojection the ratios
were still `1.91,1.17,1.31,1.78,1.09,1.16,1.18`, all worse than one.

Optimally scaling the reprojected correction no longer realizes gradient
cancellation and merely creates another one-dimensional certificate. Its
normalized capture oscillates and reaches about `0.0353` at `N=256`; proving a
uniform positive angle again requires the residual and inverse old projection
that blocked Plan 020. Plan 021 is therefore rejected, no Lean API is created,
and RH remains conditional. See
`docs/proofs/021_divisor_gradient_flow_rejection.md`.

## 2026-07-11 Plan 022 Shifted-Mobius Frame Candidate

Plan 022 is worth deeper research and has not been rejected. For each fixed
shift `1<=d<=8`, its block coefficient is

```text
1_(d divides k)*mu(k/d) - harmonicMean_(N,d),  N<k<=2N.
```

The harmonic mean makes the coefficient sum weighted by `1/k` exactly zero,
so every resulting sequence direction vanishes for all coordinates `n<=N`.
The proposed certificate uses the unprojected eight-direction Gram matrix;
because orthogonal projection only decreases its denominator, this is a
conservative lower bound for the real dyadic decrement and contains no Schur
inverse in that denominator.

The fixed `D=8` frame survives `N=128,256,512,1024,2048,4096`. At `N=4096`,
cutoff `250000`, `log(N)` times conservative normalized capture is about
`0.1657`; the frame min/max eigenvalue ratio is about `9.03e-3`, the first-`N`
coordinate leakage is `2.1e-17`, and the target normal-equation residual is
`7.8e-12`. A `D=64` robustness cohort gives about `0.2076` at the same scale.

The next mathematical bottom is an unconditional aggregate lower bound for
the eight squared residual correlations, paired with an explicit frame-energy
upper bound. A rewrite through `G_N^-1`, per-scale fitted coefficients, or a
Mertens square-root estimate is rejected. No Lean API is active until this
finite divisor-sum bound has a strict positive margin. See
`plan/022_2026-07-11_shifted_mobius_frame_plan.md` and
`docs/proofs/022_shifted_mobius_frame_first_verdict.md`.

The second 022 round selects one fixed direction inside the frame. The
eight-correlation vectors align across scales with `-mu(d)/d`, leading to the
global coefficient `Q=theta*mu`, where `theta(d)=-mu(d)/d` for `d<=8`.
Anchoring the dyadic block by one old `gamma_N` gives a sequence `h_N` that
vanishes for `n<N` without changing its correlation with `r_N`. The exact
divisor identity `1*Q=theta` collapses the untruncated divisor sum to fixed
support `1..8`.

The fixed direction survives double precision through `N=4096`; at cutoff
`250000`, `log(N)` times normalized capture is about `0.1213`, its energy is
about `0.1748`, the first-`N-1` leakage is `1.4e-17`, and the normal residual is
`7.8e-12`. Calibrated float32 rejection tests remain positive at `N=8192` and
`N=16384`. The primary proof bottom is now a uniform constant energy bound and
a `c/log N` correlation bound for this same anchored convolution.

Three shortcuts are rejected: isolating the first dyadic block ignores a
same-order far tail; the pure-new exact-orthogonal `(N,3N]` intersection loses
target capture rapidly; and the general moment-zero Bessel constant grows
linearly with `N`. See
`docs/proofs/022_fixed_convolution_second_verdict.md`.

The fixed correlation has now survived every integer scale `16<=N<=512`
without a sign change; the smallest normalized value is about `0.1029` at
`N=100`. Calibrated rejection runs remain positive through `N=16384`. This is
not pointwise positivity: bad pointwise products retain about 25--43 percent of
the good mass. The first dyadic block is positive in every tested scale and is
the candidate finite-divisor main term; the smaller far tail can oppose it, as
at `N=1024`.

No smooth scaling limit for the optimal residual block is visible. Adjacent
dyadic residual profiles are often negatively correlated. The proof must use
the exact optimality/orthogonality equations together with `1*Q=theta`, not a
continuum residual ansatz. The direct target correlations are not dominant:
the old projection component is often two to three times larger, so merely
dropping it is also rejected.

The third 022 audit identifies the fixed sequence as a centered Mertens bridge.
For `P_Q(x)=sum_(k<=x)Q(k)`, finite convolution gives
`P_Q(x)=sum_(d<=8)theta(d)M(floor(x/d))`. Because `theta(1)=-1` and
`sum_(2<=d<=8)|theta(d)|/sqrt(d)<0.758`, a standalone square-root bound for
`P_Q` would recursively give square-root Mertens control. The proposed separate
constant-energy proof is therefore rejected as an RH-level input.

Plan 022 remains active only in coupled form. On the first block,
`h_N(n)=N*S_N-(P_Q(n)-P_Q(N))`; the same centered bridge occurs in its energy
and in its correlation with `r_N`. The active theorem is the uniform

`docs/proofs/022_mertens_bridge_third_verdict.md`.

The final 022 audit rejects the route as an independent producer. For fixed
`h_N`, the normalized angle at `N=4096` is only about `0.00269` when the old
projection stops at `N/2`, then grows to `0.12684` after the full shell

The explicit multiscale space
`V_16+span(h_16,h_32,...,h_N)` does not repair this ownership failure. Its

convolution family is not dense; its positive correlation with `r_N` is

Plan 022 is rejected, no Lean API is created, and RH remains conditional. See
`docs/proofs/022_final_rejection.md`.

Plan 023 supplies an axiom-clean algebraic repair for the full-product base

```text
support(f) subset (-a,a),
Phi_f(z/(n+1)) = 1.
```

The construction interpolates `h` on the Hermitian closure of the rescaled

```text
Laplace(h*)(s) = conjugate(Laplace(h)(-conjugate(s))).
```

This is a genuine positive-definite base, not a stored positivity field. The

`docs/proofs/035_metric_projection_second_variation.md`.

The entire metric projection flow has logarithmic generator
`-U_p(I-aU_p)^-1=-sum_(m>=1)a^(m-1)U_p^m`. Hence every prime-power translation
appears before read-off; integration gives `a^m/m`, and the scaling
differential gives `m log(p)`, leaving the exact Weil coefficient
`p^(-m/2)log(p)`. Projection-interrupted words contain the nonlinear central,
boundary, and mixed-prime remainders. The arithmetic main channel is now
structurally correct to all orders; the remaining rejection test is whether
the interrupted words are trace class with only finitely many bad directions
after `Q`. See `docs/proofs/036_metric_projection_logarithmic_flow.md`.

The metric Sonin remainder now passes the operator-ideal gate, conditional on
the exact single-crossing Weil read-off. CC20 proves
`P P_hat P=R_Sonin+K_prol` with positive trace-class `K_prol` and
`Tr(K_prol) approximately 2.237484835`; its `quantsmooth` lemma makes
Schwartz-smoothed cutoff crossings trace class. A single translated crossing
has Hilbert--Schmidt norm squared `|m|log(p)norm(h)_2^2`; two crossings are
trace class, and geometric Euler coefficients dominate every polynomial
factor introduced by `Q`. Thus the finite-Euler remainder is compact relative
to the archimedean `-2 Id` essential part. The final gate is no longer
compactness but `norm(K_S)<2`, or a proof that the finite `>=2` eigenspace is
already killed by route vanishing. Arbitrary bad-vector orthogonality would
reopen the restricted-test RH exit. See
`docs/proofs/037_metric_sonin_ideal_closure.md`.

The single-crossing finite-prime read-off is now exact. For the half-line
crossing `J_b=(I-P)U_b P` and test convolution `C_h`, diagonal kernel
intersection gives `Tr(C_h* C_h J_b)=b(h* * h)(b)`. Taking
`b=m log(p)` and multiplying by the metric logarithmic-flow coefficient
`p^(-m/2)/m` yields the exact Weil atom
`p^(-m/2)log(p)(F(p^m)+F(p^-m))` for the same convolution square. Thus the
old noncompact partial translation belongs to the Weil main term rather than
the remainder. After this subtraction, only multi-crossing and
trace-class-prolate words remain. The unresolved gate is the global CC20 angle
orientation/sign and the norm of the resulting compact operator. See
`docs/proofs/038_single_crossing_weil_read_off.md`.

The finite-prime sign also matches. Metric projection variation contributes
the negative of the crossing pair, while CCM25 defines
`QW=archimedean+pole-sum_p W_p`; the local atom itself stays positive. Hence
the one-crossing metric trace and CCM25 `QW` agree in coefficient, test square,
prime-power position, and sign. No extra sign convention remains at read-off.

CCM24's de Branges realization fixes the final sign gate precisely. All
semilocal Sonin spaces map to the same vector space of entire functions, and
`upsilon_S theta_S=upsilon_infinity`; only the inner product changes. Hence
the algebraic subspace vanishing at `{0,1/2,1}` is independent of `S`.
This must not be justified by analytic pointwise invertibility of the Euler
factor, since `1-p^(-1/2-it)` vanishes at `t=i/2`. Equivalent norms do not
prove that reproducing-kernel vectors or compact bad eigenspaces stay fixed.
The last active theorem is that `-2Id+K_S` is negative on the common
triple-vanishing subspace, equivalently a certified norm bound there or
ownership of the `>=2` eigenspace by the three evaluation kernels. See
`docs/proofs/039_debranges_bad_space_gate.md`.

Plan 024 now indexes the metric Sonin projection lane as the candidate

Plan 024 is now rejected as an executable M3B lane after a source-line
common-domain audit. The positive trace-class prolate angle correction
`sum lambda_n^2 |zeta_n><zeta_n|`, whose trace is about `2.237484835`, is not
CC20's post-`Q` compact operator. Theorem `thmqkey1` instead defines an explicit
`Q delta` kernel on the convolution-root space `L2(sqrt I,d*rho)`, while the
later `E o Q` sign argument uses a distinct normalized `Q epsilon` kernel.
CCM24's `B_lambda` realizes semilocal Sonin vectors, not this test-root space.
Thus the proposed form `<F,K_S F>` for `F in B_lambda` had no same-object
operator/norm owner. The local single-crossing coefficient remains valid, but

Mellin conditions there. See
`docs/proofs/040_metric_sonin_domain_rejection.md`.

The 2026 finite Galerkin/Herglotz escape screen does not supply a new RH
producer. arXiv:2607.02828 does provide two exact reusable results: every
finite Galerkin vector maps to an explicit band-limited Guinand--Weil test with
the same cutoff-free zero sum, and the omitted post-band archimedean tail is a
strictly positive Cauchy--Stieltjes Gram increment with an explicit norm
budget. These results validate the finite coordinate system and reject
finite-cutoff negative eigenvalues inside the tail budget, but they do not
prove the cutoff-free matrix positive. Positivity of all cutoff-free matrices,
after a determining-family theorem, is Weil positivity itself. The 2026 scalar
Herglotz reduction is also not lower: it leaves one odd-sector resolvent
inequality open, while Yoshida Proposition 1(1) proves odd Weil positivity is
equivalent to RH. Finally, Yoshida Lemma 1 avoids the detector radius cycle by
allowing support to grow with the convolution power; Plan 016's fixed-window
rescaling removes exactly that freedom. The remaining honest alternatives are
an explicit global fixed-S post-Q kernel/sign theorem or a genuinely lower
arithmetic proof of the cutoff-free finite matrix signs. See
`docs/proofs/041_finite_galerkin_escape_screen.md`.

The endpoint metric Sonin projection is now mathematically rejected, beyond
the earlier common-domain objection. Pulling its trace back through `theta_S`
gives the exact same-object identity
`L_S-L_infinity=Tr(R C (I-R) H_S R (R H_S R)^-1)`. For one prime, writing
`a=p^-1/2`, `V=U+U*`, and
`A_a=(1+a^2)R-a R V R`, the correction is
`-a Tr(R C Q V R A_a^-1)`. Its second-order single-crossing term is
`-a^2 Q(U^2+U*^2)R`. Since a two-step crossing has length `2 log(p)`, this
produces `2 a^2 log(p)` times the same square evaluation, whereas the `p^2`
Weil atom has coefficient `a^2 log(p)`. The excess remains an infinite-rank
single crossing and cannot be compact. The earlier logarithmic-flow argument
missed the extra direct contribution from the moving projection factors. Keep
the local half-line trace lemma, but do not use the endpoint metric projection
as a finite-S positive trace or M3B owner. See
`docs/proofs/042_metric_sonin_second_prime_power_rejection.md`.

The cutoff-free finite Weil matrix attack now has a rigorous cancellation
verdict. Using the arXiv:2607.02828 Arb closed-form builder, interval LDL
certified positive inertia for representative matrices through dimension 129.
The project probe then reevaluated fixed high-precision minimum vectors with
Arb. At `(c,N)=(13,16)` it enclosed a positive Rayleigh quotient near
`8.5686e-35`; at `(100,16)` it enclosed one near `4.8601e-53`. Midpoint
diagnostics reach about `1.5843e-87` at `(100,32)`. Along these directions the
pole contribution is positive and order one, while the Gamma and prime
contributions are negative and cancel it to the displayed scale. This rejects
fixed coercive margins, diagonal dominance, and separate block-norm domination
as uniform proof mechanisms. The surviving coupled rank-one Krein/Herglotz
condition is exact but remains open and RH-level by the Yoshida odd-positivity
criterion. The reusable probe is
`docs/proofs/043_cutoff_free_weil_spectrum_probe.py`; the verdict is
`docs/proofs/044_cutoff_free_weil_cancellation_verdict.md`. Run WSL Arb cases
serially: concurrent WSL process fan-out triggered a service-level
`E_UNEXPECTED` unrelated to the mathematics.

The first two quantum-mechanical escape routes are rejected in their stated
forms.  For the arithmetic Lindblad proposal, matching a prime-power Weil atom
with `sqrt(w)(U-I)` forces the diagonal compensation `2w Id`.  At cutoff
`c=13`, the full compensation is about `9.9437688`, while the certified
pole-plus-Gamma Rayleigh value on the `N=16` minimum direction is only about
`0.0880103`; the required residual is therefore negative by about `9.8557585`.
Orthogonal noise channels remove cross terms but cannot remove this `J*J`
diagonal.

The ordinary prime-loop metric graph is independently rejected.  Edges of
length `log(p)` are unbounded, so fixed-width interior bumps give an infinite
orthonormal bounded-energy sequence and rule out compact resolvent for a local
self-adjoint graph Hamiltonian.  Adding dilation channels produces an open
scattering system whose prime data are resonances rather than discrete
self-adjoint eigenvalues.  A graded supertrace or nonlocal network is a new
route and receives no positivity from these rejected mechanisms.  See
`docs/proofs/045_quantum_lindblad_graph_rejection.md`.

The next original-route screen rejects four further mechanisms.  The exact
matrix-valued von Mangoldt path has positive Krein boundary masses at prime
events, but its smooth-cell cutoff curvature is indefinite; `Q_N^-1` and
`log det Q_N` have no fixed curvature either.  The coupled Schur impedance
`1/<1,Q_N^-1 1>` remains positive in the tested cells but its first and second
cutoff derivatives change sign, and it controls the even all-ones direction
rather than the odd RH gate.

The proposed `PF_infinity` Markov-cycle bridge in arXiv:2602.01248 uses a false
positive-sum closure: its determinant expansion has mixed-kernel columns.
The genuine Xi Fourier kernel cannot itself be a non-Gaussian
`PF_infinity` density because its bilateral Laplace transform is entire.
Finally, effective large-shift Jensen hyperbolicity leaves the ray
`n=0,d->infinity`, which is exactly RH.  The reusable closed-form diagnostic is
`docs/proofs/046_cutoff_schur_flow_probe.py`; the verdict is
`docs/proofs/047_original_route_rejection_screen.md`.  No new Lean owner or RH

The Robin/colossally-abundant and generic de Bruijn--Newman lanes are also
rejected as lower producers. On CA numbers, Ramanujan's RH-conditional deficit
is `Theta(1/sqrt(log n))`, while Robin's false-RH oscillation has positive
excursions `(log n)^(-b)` for some `b<1/2`. The ordinary zero-free-region PNT
error is asymptotically larger than this margin, so it cannot decide the strict
sign; proving the needed uniform sign is the RH-level gate itself. Forward
de Bruijn heat flow contracts a known zero strip and yields real zeros only at
positive time. Running it backward is not zero-preserving, while setting the
initial strip width to zero assumes RH. PF infinity is unavailable and PF5
already fails. See `docs/proofs/048_robin_heatflow_rejection.md`. No Lean owner
or route consumer changed.

The graded extension of the arithmetic Lindblad channel is now rejected as a
positive mechanism. The exact pair
`sqrt(w/2)(U-I)` and `sqrt(w/2)(U+I)` cancels the forced diagonal in supertrace
and leaves precisely `-w(U+U*)`. This is an algebraic read-off success but a
sign failure: its Fourier symbol is `-2w cos(theta)` and has both signs. More
generally, any difference of positive local `I,U` channel Gram matrices with
zero total diagonal and nonzero correlation has spectrum
`[-2|c|,+2|c|]`. Finite sums have a nonzero zero-mean trigonometric symbol and
remain indefinite; finite-codimensional route vanishing conditions cannot
remove either essential spectral side. The WSL probe is
`docs/proofs/049_graded_prime_supertrace_probe.py`; the proof verdict is
`docs/proofs/050_graded_lindblad_supertrace_rejection.md`. No Lean owner or RH
consumer changed.

The nonlocal stoquastic/gauge-Laplacian escape is rejected at the smallest
exact cutoff-free Weil matrices. The official arXiv:2607.02828 source bundle
was restored and its Arb builder rerun. At `(c,N)=(13,2)`, all 10 nonzero
triangles have positive edge-sign product; at `(13,4)`, all 84 do. A cyclic
edge product is invariant under arbitrary diagonal phases, whereas three
simultaneously nonpositive real edges would have negative product. Hence no
diagonal sign or phase gauge makes these matrices stoquastic. The same
`(13,2)` matrix remains Arb-certified positive, so this rejects only the

probe is `docs/proofs/051_stoquastic_weil_probe.py`; the verdict is
`docs/proofs/052_stoquastic_weil_gauge_rejection.md`. No Lean owner changed.

The conditional-kernel screen now imposes the actual CC20 triple vanishing on
the exact finite Guinand--Weil square tests. In the even dictionary,
`s=0,1/2,1` maps to `z=+i/2,0,-i/2`; evenness merges the endpoints.
Directly from the Volterra definition, `g_v(0)=log(c)*v_0^2`, while the source
pole-square theorem makes `g_v(i/2)=0` exactly the pole-neutral linear row.
Thus the same-object coefficient subspace is `v_0=0` intersected with that
row, not the paper's moment-neutral condition.

Arb compression at `c=13`, `N=4,8,16` certifies positive total inertia on
dimensions `3,7,15`, with midpoint minimum scales about `1.40e-6`, `3.86e-14`,
and `7.42e-25`. The pole block vanishes exactly, but Gamma has one negative
direction near `-0.25` at every level and the prime block has growing negative
inertia with minimum midpoint reaching about `-5.47e4`. Triple vanishing
therefore does not produce separate positive kernels; only the full coupled
Gamma--prime cancellation remains, which is the constrained Weil sign itself.
An independent `c=29,N=8` run has the same outcome: positive total inertia,
two negative Gamma directions, and four negative prime directions.
See `docs/proofs/053_triple_vanishing_weil_probe.py` and
`docs/proofs/054_triple_vanishing_conditional_kernel_verdict.md`. No Lean owner
or consumer changed.

The coupled finite Weil source has an exact Loewner shape but rejects the
standard operator-monotone escape. If `psi_c` is its odd divided-difference
source and `Phi_c(x)=sqrt(x)*psi_c(sqrt(x))`, the positive-frequency even block
is twice the Loewner matrix of `Phi_c` on square nodes. Arb verifies this
identity on the `1^2,...,4^2` off-diagonal entries. Yet the same official
closed forms certify `Phi_c(1/4)>Phi_c(1)` by about `0.7641`, `1.3945`, and
`3.0139` at cutoffs `c=13,29,100`. Since operator-monotone and complete
Bernstein functions are scalar nondecreasing, no positive-measure Loewner
representation proves this source positive. Positive finite node matrices do
not contradict this continuous failure. See
`docs/proofs/055_loewner_bernstein_probe.py` and
`docs/proofs/056_loewner_bernstein_rejection.md`. No Lean owner changed.

The lattice-only Bernstein/Stieltjes fallback also fails before any spectral
claim. For `a_n=Phi_c(n^2)`, a discrete Bernstein measure would force ordinary
increments to decrease, while a positive squared-node Stieltjes measure would
force adjacent secant slopes in `n^2` to decrease. Arb proves both grow already
from nodes `1,2,3`. The square-secant growth is about `0.0042444`, `0.0025804`,
and `0.00084713` for `c=13,29,100`; all intervals are strictly positive.
An `N`-dependent rational Pick interpolant reconstructed after a positive LDL
is only an equivalent finite positivity certificate and supplies no common
arithmetic measure. See `docs/proofs/057_discrete_bernstein_probe.py` and
`docs/proofs/058_discrete_bernstein_rejection.md`. No Lean owner changed.

The fixed-cutoff band-growth Schur route is also rejected in its inverse-based
form. Reflection splits `Q_N` into nested even and odd blocks, so each new
frequency has scalar pivot `s_N=a_N-b_N^T A_(N-1)^-1 b_N`. Arb certifies all
tested pivots positive through `(c,N)=(13,16)` and `(29,8)`, but the inverse
correction cancels the new diagonal by up to 15 decimal orders. At `c=29,N=8`,
the even ratio `s_N/a_N` is about `1.10e-15` and the odd ratio is about
`1.82e-14`; pivots also oscillate with `N`.

Algebraically the parity blocks are Loewner matrices of
`Phi(x)=sqrt(x)psi(sqrt(x))` and, up to diagonal factors,
`Chi(x)=psi(sqrt(x))/sqrt(x)`. Their rank-two displacement identity holds for
arbitrary sign-indefinite sources and gives no positivity. Calling the Schur
pivot an RKHS residual norm assumes old-kernel positivity; the determinant
ratio is equivalent to the same PSD induction. No inverse-free arithmetic
square identity survived. See `docs/proofs/059_parity_schur_band_probe.py` and
`docs/proofs/060_parity_schur_inverse_rejection.md`. No Lean owner changed.

A source-backed pole-free constraint route survives the latest rejection

Same-object Arb compression shows that mean-zero `v_0=0` alone retains the

critical quantity `1+2G(0)` is only `10^-15` to `10^-35`. Thus `G(0)<0` has a
stable sign margin and is a distinct intermediate target.

The soft mean-zero estimate using `min J` fails: Arb values of
`2aJ(2a)+kappa_a(0)` range from about `-2.81` at `c=5` to `-10.72` at `c=100`.
The active analytic gate is instead the zero-energy anti-maximum statement
`A_tilde^-1 C<0`, or an equivalent proof that `A_tilde` is nonnegative on

index-one statement remains unproved. See
`docs/proofs/061_polefree_poincare_probe.py`,
`docs/proofs/062_polefree_constraint_resolvent_probe.py`, and
`docs/proofs/063_polefree_constraint_survivor.md`. No Lean owner changed.

The pole-free constraint candidate is now rejected as an executable lower

Suzuki Section 8 retains the nonlocal screw operator in the generalized
problem `G_a u=lambda(-Delta_N)^-1u`; its use of `lambda=0` explicitly begins

The next diagonal death test did not reject the corrected M3A kernel. From the

2026-07-12 Q-root Mellin gate: with
`laplaceAt(f,s)=integral exp(s*x)f(x)`, compact-support integration by parts

2026-07-12 Plan 025 Xi-kernel reduction: in centered log coordinates,
`psi(x)=exp(x/2)*completedRiemannXiKernel(exp(2x))` is even. Its first
derivative jump at zero is `-1`, so `psi''` contains `-delta_0`; the `+1` in
`completedRiemannXi=(u^2-1/4)completedRiemannZeta0+1` contributes the opposite
Dirac mass. Thus the centered Xi inverse is the ordinary function
`psi''-psi/4`. If `H(z)=0`, division by `s-z` has inverse
`exp(-zx)*integral_[x,infinity] exp(zy)phi(y)dy`; the zero moment also gives
the left-tail formula and cancels the homogeneous exponential. See
`docs/proofs/075_centered_xi_kernel_delta_cancellation.md`.

2026-07-12 Plan 025 convention/sign gates: centered variable `u=s-1/2`
aligns additive involution `u -> -conjugate(u)` with the source orbit
`s -> 1-conjugate(s)`. The current `logPullbackRaw=g(exp x)` is uncentered and
cannot be reused; a future owner must include the half-density factor. On the

along the two involution pairs gives a strictly negative square zero-sum.
Multiplication by `u*(u^2-1/4)` adds the route zeros and stays nonzero on the
target orbit. See proof records 076 and 077.

2026-07-12 Plan 025 compact-cutoff reduction: if the iterated Xi-orbit
quotient inverse has uniform weighted derivative tails, integration by parts

channels by one nested half-line channel gives `C_ij=min(log p_i,log p_j)` and

`w^T C^(-1)w = w_1^2/b_1 + sum (Delta w_i)^2/Delta b_i`. With
`w(b)=exp(-b/2)`, secant Cauchy-Schwarz yields the cofinal bound
`1/(2 log 2)+1/8 = 0.846347... < 1`. Direct computations for 1, 5, 20, 80,
and 120 primes agree and approach `0.846`. This is the first candidate to pass
the cofinal Schur-cost gate. Remaining bottoms are a same-square boundary-data
Gram estimate and a trace read-off without mixed-prime terms. No Lean owner is
authorized yet. See proof 133 and `docs/proofs/133_shared_brownian_gram_probe.py`.

2026-07-13 inverse-log metric projection rejection:
Proof 205 proposed, for finite `S_f`,

```text
ell_S=sum_p log((I-p^(-1/2)U_p)^*(I-p^(-1/2)U_p)),
b_S=sum_p 2log(1+p^(-1/2)),
H_S=((1+b_S)I-ell_S)^(-1).
```

The scalar `b_S` does give `0<H_S<=I`, and the no-internal-`Q` subseries is
formally

```text
Q(I-H_S^(-1))R=Q ell_S R.
```

Proof 206 rejects the inference that the complementary words have two boundary
crossings. The exact block formula is

```text
Q H_S R(R H_S R)^(-1)
  =((1+b_S)Q-Q ell_S Q)^(-1)Q ell_S R.
```

For one prime its difference from `Q ell R` is

```text
a^2(2Q(U+U*)R+Q(U+U*)Q(U+U*)R)+O(a^3).
```

Translation parity isolates the first term as a genuine one-step crossing. On
the `log(p)` fiber decomposition its `(-1,0)` block is
`(2a^2+O(a^3))I` on `L2([0,log(p)))`, so it is noncompact. The WSL finite
section confirms the coefficient ratio tends to `2`; the proof uses the exact
expansion, not the numerics. Plan 046 is rejected before Wiener summability or
domain transport. No Lean owner was created and no RH root was removed.

2026-07-13 pole-free cosh and endpoint-collar verdict:
The source jump-form potential was evaluated without replacing its endpoint
geometry by a grid. For `C(x)=cosh(x/2)`, the complete-graph Picone minorant has
the exact center margin

```text
gamma_C+(A_tilde C)(0)/C(0),
```

and Arb proves it strictly negative at `c=5,13,29,53,100,1000,10000`; the
values run from about `-2.99069` to `-105.020`. This rejects that global
minorant, not the full jump geometry.

In the final endpoint indicator cell, `x=a-d`, the potential has the exact
stable formula

```text
kappa_a(a-d)
 = -(1/2)log(d(2a-d))-log(2*pi)-EulerGamma
   -F(d)-F(2a-d)-sum_(q<c) Lambda(q)/sqrt(q).
```

Its derivative is `J(2a-d)-J(d)<0`, so there is one collar root. Arb brackets
that root at seven cutoffs: the widths are approximately `1.329e-4`,
`2.511e-7`, `1.807e-10`, `5.506e-14`, `1.306e-18`, `1.308e-56`, and
`1.314e-175` for `c=5,13,29,53,100,1000,10000`. Partial summation gives the
scale `-log d_c=4 sqrt(c)+o(sqrt(c))`. Directly evaluating
`d(2a-d)` is essential; forming `a^2-(a-d)^2` loses all useful digits at the
large cutoffs.

A single translated collar root has prime-free convolution square once
`d_c<log 2`. Proof 113 then makes the same M4/pole-neutral test strictly
QW-positive, so it cannot be the required negative detector. A two-collar
class is not rejected by this argument, but no determining theorem or
same-object finite-S read-off exists. See proof 208 and its Arb script.

```text
B_(r,s)(a)=P_r v_a^*(1-P_s)v_a P_r,
```

```text
b_(r,s)(a)=sum_m |c_m|^2(s-r-m log p)_+.
```

strictly positive central coefficient.  Nested support compressions are not
operator-monotone because the compression difference has a zero diagonal block

`B_alpha'=[K_alpha,B_alpha]`, so Kato transport gives one exact unitary path
from `B_0` to `B_alpha`. The resolvent expansion

```text
X_alpha=-sum_(m>=1)alpha^(m-1)U^m
```

is uniformly norm summable for `alpha<=p^(-1/2)<=1/sqrt(2)`. This removes
separate principal `m log(p)` and amplitude Euler summability from the active
bottom: their large diagonal endpoint pieces cancel before the complete flow
is formed. The deterministic certificates pass at `p=2,3`; at `p=2` the
separated phase and defect diagonal derivative norms are both about `16.41`,
while the recombined diagonal error is about `1.6e-15`.

instantaneous flow is indefinite. Abstract nesting or monotonicity cannot
prove the sign. The remaining compactness theorem is one local
Hilbert--Schmidt estimate for `Y_alpha+Y_alpha*` on the same Q-root, integrable
in `alpha`. The integrated three-row sign and RH remain open. No Lean owner
was added.

```text
a^m k_infinity(r+q_m)
```

The complex phase operator on a bounded log interval has kernel

```text
exp((x-y)/2)exp(2pi i lambda exp(x-y)).
```

summability is false but unnecessary. The negative translated endpoint keeps

operator norm is `0.0625=2^(-4)` while its HS norm remains about `0.7071068`.

2026-07-14 complete principal Euler-profile compactness:
Proof 229 sums the normalized triangular widths before applying post-Q. The
exact Euler envelope

```text
W_p(r)=sum_(m>=1)p^(-m/2)(m log(p)-r)_+
```


integrations by parts transfer the post-Q derivatives off the fast phase. The
first boundary family cancels exactly by envelope continuity. The cell
interiors are HS-summable with majorant `p^(-n/2)`. The remaining derivative
jumps have size `p^(-n/2)` and acquire Proof 228's second `p^(-n/2)`
operator-norm gain, so their compact chirp series is summable as `p^(-n)`.

finite root interval. It need not be Hilbert--Schmidt. Proof 227's single
global L2-kernel contract is sufficient but unnecessarily strong; the sharp

boundary. WSL algebraic certificates pass at `p=2,3,101`; their envelope,
continuity, and derivative-jump errors are below `4.5e-16`.

Proof 230 gives an exact C*-algebra quotient theorem for the nonconstant metric
part. Let `r<=e`, `b=e-r`, `T=I-alpha u`, and let `Phi_T(p)` be the orthogonal


defect square, and Kato re-orthogonalization cannot create a new quotient
class outside the source commutator.

compactness theorem is generator stability of Proofs 228--229's profile class

2026-07-16 positive heat and diagonal joint-torsion cancellation:
Proof 299 factors Proof 298's ordered relative Gram determinant into a
positive symmetric covariance determinant and a central anomaly determinant.
With

```text
A_s=(B exp(sW)B)^(1/2),
Gamma_sym(s)=A_s Gamma A_s,
```

the anomaly factor is

```text
J(s)=Gamma_sym(s)Gamma^(-1)(B exp(sW)B)^(-1),

det J(s)=d(A_s,Gamma)^(-1).
```

Here `d` is the determinant invariant of an almost-commuting Fredholm pair.
Finite matrices force this determinant to one, but Proof 264's infinite shift
guard has central physical anomalies `0.175/0.225` in the two Proof 299
cohorts.  Never infer `J=I` or `det J=1` from finite sections.

The route diagonal has an extra owner which the abstract guard lacks.  Proof
263 makes `Q_S(g,g)` real, while Proof 265 makes its centered numerator `N`
trace class.  Thus

```text
N_sym=(N+N*)/2,
N_anom=(N-N*)/2,

Tr(N_sym Gamma^-1) is real,
Tr(N_anom Gamma^-1) is purely imaginary.
```

Their sum is the real source response, so the diagonal anomaly first jet is
exactly zero.  Consequently

```text
Q_S(g,g)
 =Tr(N_sym Gamma^-1)
 =partial_s log det(
    K*exp(sW)K Gamma_sym(s)^(-1))|_(s=0).
```

This does not say that the anomaly determinant is constant, and it does not
apply directly to cross roots.  Prove the diagonal bound first and use Proof
263 polarization afterward.

Carey--Pincus 1979 relates principal functions of analytic almost-periodic

motion of Dirichlet series. Sugahara 2026 gives a modern Hardy-Toeplitz
Helton--Howe measure formula. A later symmetry audit rejects this as the Gate

antisymmetric commutator `C^dagger-C`, while the completed orthogonal flow is
the symmetric response `C+C^dagger`. The active missing object is therefore a
relative symmetric semicommutator distribution for the actual Gram-corrected
`E/R/K_prol` owner, or the matching mixed second variation of the relative
Fredholm cocycle. Generic Helton--Howe variation is forbidden both because it
has the wrong symmetry and because a branchwise trace norm loses the relative
cancellation.

Proof 375 identifies the actual source Sonin range, in the ordinary common-log
Fourier/Mellin coordinate, as a closed nearly invariant Hardy subspace.  The
completed Mellin range is Burnol's de Branges space; division by its
Hermite--Biehler function gives a model space, and return to the ordinary
Plancherel coordinate gives an isometric multiplier range.  CCM24's causal
finite-Euler transport is a bounded invertible analytic multiplier, so every
actual prefix range remains nearly invariant.  This does not identify an
Euler weight with a semilocal Hermite--Biehler generator.

Proof 376 proves the uniform projection-commutator theorem for any scalar
nearly invariant disk Hardy subspace `M`.  Hitt--Sarason gives `M=g K_I` with
an isometric multiplier and Hartmann--Ross gives the orthogonal projection
formula.  Commuting the Cayley coordinate multiplier through that formula
reduces `[M_z,P_M]` to the model-space defect and gives rank at most two.
Telescoping powers gives

```text
rank([M_(z^n),P_M])<=2 abs(n),
norm([M_(z^n),P_M])_2<=sqrt(2 abs(n)).
```

Consequently, if

```text
A(c)=sum_(n !=0)sqrt(abs(n)) abs(c_n)<infinity,
```

then `norm([M_c,P_M])_2<=sqrt(2)A(c)`, uniformly in the range and the Euler
prefix.  No extremal-multiplier norm or Gram inverse occurs.

Proof 377 transfers a compact logarithmic convolution root through the Cayley
boundary coordinate.  Circle `H^2`, Cauchy--Schwarz, the exact first two Cayley
derivatives, Plancherel, and compact support give

```text
sum_(n !=0)sqrt(abs(n)) abs(c_n)
 <=C(1+B_root)^2 norm(g)_(H^3).
```

Together with Proofs 375--376 and the direct outer half-line estimate, this
proves

```text
 <=C(1+B_root)^4 norm(g)_(H^3)^2.                  (MR.6)
```

```text
Burnol, Sonine spaces and de Branges, Theorem 8:
https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0208121

Hartmann--Ross, nearly invariant subspaces, Section 2 and Lemma 2.4:
https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.3771

Consani--Moscovici, semilocal Sonin transport, Theorem 4.6:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18423
```

Proof 381 proves that the uniform endpoint theorem cannot supply a common
right factor by abstract functional analysis.  On `L2(T)=ell2(Z)`, take

```text
M_N=K_(z^N)=span(e_0,...,e_(N-1)),
D_N=[M_z,P_(M_N)].
```

Then

```text

D_N e_(N-1)=e_N,
rank(D_N)=2,
norm(D_N)=1,
norm(D_N)_2=sqrt(2)
```

for every `N`.  If `D_N=B_N A` for one Hilbert--Schmidt `A` and uniformly
bounded `B_N`, then `norm(A e_(N-1))` is bounded below uniformly.  Its squared
column norms cannot be summable, a contradiction.  Therefore uniform rank,
operator norm, and `S_2` estimates do not imply one common Douglas owner.
The actual route must use compact real-line boundary localization and its one
fixed Burnol source.

invertible multipliers give equivalences of generalized Toeplitz operators,

```text

https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05453
```

2026-07-20 Proof 422 audited the proposed infinite CAR/quasi-free lift of Proof
421 and rejected the standard per-state centering under the route's current
trace-ideal hypotheses.  Avron--Bachmann--Graf--Klich Propositions 5--6
(`https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.0099`) show that, for a projection sea `P` and a
bounded self-adjoint detector `W`, `[P,W] in S2` produces an implementing
generator.  Its vacuum-centered normalization is unique, but every other
generator differs by `c_P I`.  Thus fixed-state CAR determines centered
fluctuations, not a relative first moment between independently represented
seas.

Matsui--Yamagami Theorem 2.1
(`https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3581`) says that pure projection quasi-free states
for `P,Q` are quasi-equivalent exactly when `P-Q in S2`; Theorem 3.3 gives the
disjointness alternative.  The pure-state full-counting-statistics theorem of
Avron et al. assumes the stronger raw transport condition `P-U P U* in S1`.
Proof 261 owns only the root-sandwiched statement

```text
C_eta(B_1-B_0)C_xi* in S1,
```

so neither standard theorem applies to the moving Burnol band without a new
raw ideal theorem.

The exact continuous guard uses

```text
H=L2(R),
E=M_(1_[0,infinity)),
E_b=M_(1_[b,infinity)),
D_b=E-E_b=M_(1_[0,b)),
b>0.
```

`D_b` is an infinite-rank projection and is not compact, so the two quasi-free
states are disjoint.  For nonzero `g in C_c^infinity(R)`, however,

```text
norm(C_g D_b)_2^2=b norm(g)_2^2,

C_g(E-E_b)C_g* in S1,
Tr(C_g(E-E_b)C_g*)=b norm(g)_2^2>0.
```

With `W=C_g* C_g`, the half-line commutator satisfies

```text
norm([W,E])_2^2
 =integral_R abs(z) abs((g^star*g)(z))^2 dz<infinity.
```

Thus a centered detector implementer exists in both endpoint GNS spaces.  Since
`W` commutes with translations, the two centered spectral laws are identical;
all centered cumulants and Fisher distances agree, even though the root-
completed relative first moment above is positive.  Shifting one generator by
`b norm(g)_2^2 I` restores that first moment only by inserting the unknown
normal-ordering phase.  This is the same first-cumulant anomaly retained by
Proofs 264, 415, and 420.

The surviving probability route is therefore a cutoff-before-limit theorem on
one common finite carrier.  It must prove simultaneously: convergence of the
finite relative mean to `Tr(C_g(B_1-B_0)C_g*)`; a cutoff-independent detector-
variance bound; and a canonical Fisher-action bound by
`C_lambda(1+B_F)^d E(S_F)`.  Separately centered infinite CAR laws cannot be
cited as that limit.  The direct alternative remains Proof 416 `(EN.7)` on the
completed Burnol boundary form.  No numerical certificate or Lean source was
needed for Proof 422; the proof is the trace-ideal calculation and the two
primary-source contracts.  Proof 416's `3700`-job build remains the latest Lean
acceptance.  Gate 3U, the finite-`S` sign, the same-object arithmetic identity,
Burnol's identity, and RH remain open.  See
`docs/proofs/422_car_common_normal_ordering_boundary.md`.

2026-07-20 Proof 424 audited the common-cutoff probability successor from
Proofs 421--422.  The new Lean module

```text
CCM24FiniteSCutoffTraceAnomaly.lean
```

defines literal finite coordinate projections and proves

```text
Tr(W P_S)=card(S) kappa
```

when the detector diagonal is the constant `kappa`.  It also proves that
finite similarity by a transport commuting with `W` leaves the detector trace
unchanged.  Thus translated equal-rank windows have zero response at every
cutoff: their physical `+b kappa` boundary is canceled by an artificial
`-b kappa` far boundary.  Using one common physical far endpoint retains the
correct response but changes the projection rank by `b`, so it cannot enter
Proof 421's differentiable fixed-rank projection-DPP score.

This does not reject every equal-rank cutoff.  One can pad the target with
modes escaping to a detector-invisible region.  Such padding breaks
translation covariance and becomes a new detector-dependent boundary datum;
strong convergence alone proves neither its anomaly limit nor its Fisher
bound.

Proof 424 then gives an exact fixed-size no-go for the proposed localization.
On `M` disjoint pairs, rotate one occupied frame vector from `e_j` to `f_j`
and use weights

```text
w(e_j)=3^(-j),
w(f_j)=0.
```

The fixed-size projection DPP is a product of `M` Bernoulli choices.  The
ternary statistic `X_w=sum 3^(-j)B_j` determines all bits, so

```text
E[score|X_w]=score.
```

Along the sharp Fisher--Rao path `p(t)=cos^2(pi*t/2)`, the endpoint response is
less than `1/2`, the integrated detector variance is less than `1/64`, but
the detector-conditional Fisher action is exactly `M*pi^2`.  Positive
summable detector weights therefore do not make exact-statistic conditioning
cutoff independent.  Scaling the weights does not change the generated
sigma-algebra.

A variable-size positive-contraction DPP can carry a rank change, but the
canonical Bernoulli interpolation has the sharp lower bound `pi^2` per
removed mode.  On increasing finite-dimensional subspaces of the continuous
half-line defect its raw Fisher action diverges.  The root-completed first
moment remains finite, so a surviving probability proof must construct both a
detector-relative boundary completion and a stable coarse graining, then
identify its first moment with the actual completed Burnol trace before
estimating Fisher energy.  Projecting the score only onto the linear span of
`X_w-E X_w` is stable but returns
`abs(d E X_w/dt)^2/Var(X_w)`, the original signed response estimate.

No numerical experiment was needed.  The finite trace guard is Lean-owned;
the DPP and Fisher guards are exact Bernoulli algebra.  The direct active

2026-07-20 Proof 426 audited the remaining possibility of importing an
almost-periodic strong Szego--Widom theorem for Proof 416's canonical Euler
family.  Zhou's uniform theorem
(`https://escholarship.org/uc/item/2fq9h2v6`) assumes a weighted Wiener algebra
over a finitely generated frequency group.  Proposition 4.1.6 constructs a
compatible polynomial weight from a Diophantine lower bound, Example 4.1.8
uses Baker--Feldman for logarithms of algebraic numbers, and Theorem 4.1.9 gives
the fixed-group determinant asymptotic.  The uniform formula keeps two
boundary functions `Theta_(A,1)(tau_(n_1))` and
`Theta_(A,2)(tau_(n_2))`; the source leaves their phase differentiability as
an open question.

Proof 426 proves a missing quantitative lower bound.  For `n` rationally
independent frequencies in `R/Z`, place the `(Q+1)^n` points from the integer
box `{0,...,Q}^n` on the circle.  Two have distance at most `(Q+1)^(-n)`.
Their nonzero difference has sup norm at most `Q`, so any lower bound

```text
norm(alpha dot xi)_(R/Z)
 >=C(1+norm(alpha)_infinity)^(-omega)
```

forces `omega>=n`.  Distinct frequencies `log(p)/(2 pi)` are rationally
independent: a relation would equate a rational prime product with
`exp(2 pi k)`; unique factorization handles `k=0` and Gelfond--Schneider rules
out `k!=0`.

The canonical visible set can realize the large-rank case.  If `g_B` is a
nonnegative smooth bump supported in `[-B,B]` and positive inside, its
autocorrelation is positive for every displacement of absolute value less
than `2B`.  Its exact prime-power support therefore contains every prime below
`exp(2B)`, so the compatible exponent is at least
`pi(exp(2B))~exp(2B)/(2B)`.  This cost is unrelated to Proof 416's
`O((1+B)^2)` diagonal Euler energy.

The existing almost-periodic theorem can still apply to one fixed finite
frequency group after choosing a compatible weight and endpoint phases.  It
cannot yield a fixed support-polynomial Sobolev order or constant over the
support-coupled canonical families, and it does not estimate the
root-relative detector derivative.  The endpoint-phase dependence is the
finite-section form of Proof 425's normal-ordering ambiguity.  Proof 426 uses
an exact analytic argument and adds no Lean source or numerical certificate.

2026-07-20 Proof 429 repaired a formal-integrity defect in the fixed-`S`
trace owner and completed the literal carrier instantiation of Proof 428.
The source module `CCM24FiniteSCommonBoundaryPair.lean` still contained three

of the complete common pair, and its trace-product readback.  Inspection of

```text

```

so the independent reflected-outer contribution had no coordinate.  The old
reflected pair also used the reflected compact root, although the physical
ledger makes the reflected outer term the negative adjoint of the ordinary
outer term.  The reflected compact root belongs to the second-support branch.

The repaired carrier is the balanced orthogonal sum

```text
(outer + reflected-outer) + (second-support + prolate).
```

The reflected pair is now exactly
`(outerCommutatorPairData ...).swap.smulRight (-1)`.  Its trace product is the
negative adjoint of the ordinary outer branch.  Nested `l2Sum` then constructs
the complete pair, and its trace product is the actual
`cc20ThreeBranchCommutator`.  The historical `three branch` name counts the
outer algebraic branch once even though it has two physical orientations.
All three placeholders were removed.

specializes that owner to the actual normalized finite-Euler inverse.  It

```text
sourceBandEulerFixedQuotient_ordinaryTrace_norm_le_of_currentRangeReadout
sourceBandEulerFixedQuotient_ordinaryTrace_norm_le_of_currentRangeDomination
sourceBandEulerFixedQuotient_ordinaryTrace_norm_le_of_currentRangeNormSqDomination
```

These theorems are valid abstract adapters, but a second inspection showed
that they are not the physical Euler producer.  Their Julia defect steps act
on the packed four-coordinate boundary root.  The genuine suffix-generated
Euler schedule instead acts on `sourceSoninCarrier`.

Proof 432 repairs that second mismatch with the literal rectangular input

```text
sourceBandFiniteEulerSoninInput
```

The generic
`inputSideRectangularJuliaReadout_ordinaryTrace_norm_le` theorem keeps the
band input, packed compact root, source Sonin Julia input, and packed output as
four separate Hilbert carriers.  Its route-facing specialization

```text
sourceBandEulerFixedQuotient_ordinaryTrace_norm_le_of_actualCurrentRangeReadout
```

forces the exact schedule

```text
currentRangeJuliaSteps
  (fixedSourceCurrentRangeJuliaSteps lambda stepData S).
```

The theorem initially hit a deterministic `whnf` timeout at
`1000000` heartbeats.  The proof now gives `H/K/D/G` explicitly and
shares the actual step list, rectangular input, readout map, and readout bound
as local definitions.  The declaration alone uses a scoped
`maxHeartbeats 2000000`; no global option was added.  With that local budget,
the source module builds in about 107 seconds in the cached WSL verification
copy.

The consumer leaves exactly two honest source obligations:

```text
1. completed physical right column
     = fixed-source readout of the actual suffix Julia range column;

2. that actual Julia range column is square-summable along the band basis,
   with the eventual support-polynomial bound uniform in the visible set.
```

The first obligation is not already encoded by the step-data type.
`SuffixPrimeEulerProjectedJuliaSchurFrameStepData.fixedSourceReadout` is an
independent field.  Its existing `rangeSine_readback` theorem constrains the
different ambient `readout` field.  Therefore a supplied suffix schedule
does not imply the physical right-column equality.  The second obligation must
retain the localized Julia range maps: replacing it by Hilbert--Schmidt
summability of the raw map `J_R* E A_S E J_B` would be stronger and would
discard the compact boundary localization.

The current primary-source audit found no shortcut.  Connes' 2026 survey
`https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04022` presents finite-to-infinite Euler
convergence/positivity as a proposed strategy.  Alpay--Colombo--Lewkowicz--
Sabadini, `https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05334`, Theorem 4.1 assumes a pair
of unitary operators whose resolvent difference has fixed finite rank.  The
route instead has a nonunitary bounded-invertible Euler transport and only
compact-root-sandwiched trace-class differences, so that theorem supplies
neither missing producer.

2026-07-20 Proof 433 removes the Julia readout as a necessary estimator for
the literal normalized finite-Euler fixed-quotient first jet.  Proof 432 had
correctly isolated a rectangular physical input

```text
J_R* E A_S E J_B : Ran(E-R) -> Ran(R),
```

but its consumer then required the physical right column to factor through an
actual suffix Julia range column and required that stronger column to be
square-summable.  Inspection of the complete producer showed a shorter ideal
route.  Before the quotient carrier change, all four physical coordinates are
already assembled as one Hilbert--Schmidt pair

```text
fixedPhysicalPairData=(L_phys,R_phys).
```

The quotient first jet only forms

```text
L_S=L_phys B*,
R_S=R_phys R(E A_S E)B,
```

and then precomposes both legs with the isometric band inclusion `J_B`.
Here `B`, `R`, `E`, `J_B`, and the Markov-normalized inverse `A_S` all have
operator norm at most one.  The new module

```text
ConnesWeilRH/Source/CCM25Concrete/
  CCM24FiniteSFixedQuotientContractionBound.lean
```

proves quantitative square-energy monotonicity for both legs of
`boundedSandwich` and `boundedPrecomp`, proves

```text
norm(sourceBandFiniteEulerSoninInput lambda family)<=1,
```

and derives the family-independent trace estimate

```text
abs Tr(Q_S^jet)
 <=1/2 [
      sum_i norm(L_phys e_i)^2
     +sum_i norm(R_phys e_i)^2
   ].
```

No physical branch is normed separately: the balanced
`(outer+reflected-outer)+(second-support+prolate)` pair stays whole until the
two completed Hilbert--Schmidt legs are paired.  The result therefore avoids
both the carrier error from Proof 431 and the abstract Julia kernel-alignment
obstruction from Proof 388.

The semantic limit is equally important.  This is a bound for the literal
fixed-quotient first-jet owner only.  It neither supplies a
support-polynomial Sobolev estimate for the fixed physical square energy nor
identifies that first jet with Proof 415's completed Burnol weighted endpoint
or Proof 429's target-commutator response.  The remaining arrows are

```text
fixed physical square energy
  -> selected-root support/Sobolev bound;

fixed-quotient first jet
  -> complete Burnol endpoint on the same object.
```

Thus Proof 432's Julia premises remain valid sufficient adapters but are not
the minimum estimator for this first jet.  Proof 433 does not claim that the
raw map `J_R* E A_S E J_B` is Hilbert--Schmidt and does not close Gate 3U,
the finite-`S` sign, Burnol's identity, or RH.

2026-07-20 Proof 434 replaces Proof 433's nonhomogeneous additive energy by
an exact root-completed Hilbert--Schmidt owner.  The obstruction is scaling:
under `g -> epsilon g`, the detector `C_g* C_g` and the actual first-jet
response scale by `|epsilon|^2`, while the old fixed physical square energy
contains a prolate coordinate which is not scaled by both detector roots.
That valid additive trace bound therefore cannot be the target of the desired
homogeneous support--Sobolev estimate.

The new module

```text
ConnesWeilRH/Source/CCM25Concrete/
  CCM24FiniteSRootCompletedFirstJet.lean
```

splits the compressed detector before any square energy is taken.  With

```text
B   =sourceBandProjection,
P   =sourceSoninProjection,
Q   =sourceFourierSupportProjection,
L_g =E C_g*,
R_g =C_g E,
N_S =E A_S E,
```

Lean proves the exact same-object identity

```text
B [L_g R_g,P] P N_S B

 =B Q L_g R_g P N_S B
  +B(I-Q)L_g[R_g,Q]P N_S B
  +B(I-Q)[L_g,Q]R_g P N_S B.
```

Every term contains both convolution roots exactly once.  The three branch
pairs are

```text
A_0=(B Q L_g)*,               D_0=R_g P N_S B,
A_1=(B(I-Q)L_g)*,             D_1=[R_g,Q]P N_S B,
A_2=(B(I-Q)[L_g,Q])*,         D_2=D_0.
```

`sourceRootCompletedPairData` combines them in one balanced orthogonal
`WithLp` carrier.  Its trace product is definitionally the actual
`sourceRootCompletedFixedQuotientCorner`, and the earlier finite-Euler corner
is proved equal to that owner.  Infinite Holder with exponents `2,2` gives
the multiplicative bound

```text
abs Tr(first jet)
 <=sqrt(E(A_0)+E(A_1)+E(A_2))
   sqrt(E(D_0)+E(D_1)+E(D_0)).
```

The two `l2Sum` energy readbacks are proved explicitly, so the five remaining
analytic obligations are visible and no unscaled prolate energy is hidden in
the pair carrier.

Proof 434 also proves a general continuous compact-kernel estimate

```text
sum_i norm(T_k e_i)^2
 <=measure(Y) measure(X) supNorm(k)^2.
```

Specializing with `SchwartzMap.norm_le_seminorm` gives, for a root supported
in `[a,c]`, `d=c-a`, and its `0,0` Schwartz seminorm `s_00`,

```text
E(negativeBoundaryRootKernel) <=d^2 s_00^2,
E(positiveBoundaryRootKernel) <=d^2 s_00^2,
E(fullBoundaryRootKernel)     <=2 d^2 s_00^2.
```

These are actual compact boundary kernels already used by the physical
crossing construction.  The new theorem does not yet identify all five maps
`A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1` as bounded sandwiches of those kernels, nor prove the
complete family-uniform polynomial bound for their geometric energy.  The
same-object bridge from this fixed-quotient first jet to the completed Burnol
weighted endpoint also remains open.  Therefore Gate 3U, the finite-`S` sign,
Burnol's identity, and RH remain open.

telescope from Hilbert--Schmidt to trace class.  For every nonzero circle
mode,

```text
rank([z^n,P_M])<=2|n|,
norm([z^n,P_M])<=1,
norm([z^n,P_M])_1<=2|n|.
```

Consequently, for `c=sum_n c_n z^n`,

```text
norm([M_c,P_M])_1<=2 sum_(n!=0)|n||c_n|.
```

Proof 377's Cayley `H^2` calculation also controls this stronger coefficient
functional:

```text
sum_(n!=0)|n||c_n|
 <=C(1+B_root)^2 norm(g)_(H^3).
```

The detector Leibniz rule

```text
[C* C,P]=C*[C,P]+[C*,P]C
```

and Young's convolution bound then give

```text
norm([W,P])_1
 <=C_0(1+B_root)^3 norm(g)_(H^3)^2.
```

```text
abs Tr(J_S)
 <=C_0(1+B_root)^3 norm(g)_(H^3)^2
```

uniformly in every finite `S`.  This is stronger than the support-coupled
canonical quantifier required by Proof 435.  It respects Proof 260 because
the trace norm is taken only after the entire fixed source commutator has
recombined; no renewal atom is placed under an absolute value.

The module defines the literal root-smoothed complete crossing
`actualCompletedRootCrossing`.  It consumes
`rootSandwiched_completedMovingCrossing_eq_neg_soninCrossing` and
`actualMovingSoninRootFlow_eq_crossing_add_adjoint` to prove, for every
`|alpha| <= 1`,

```text
actualMovingSoninRootFlow owner lambda alpha S
  = -actualCompletedRootCrossing owner lambda alpha S
    - actualCompletedRootCrossing owner lambda alpha S^*.
```

This is the exact order needed by the route: the radial generator invariance
deletes the outer crossing before any integration or norm.  The five physical
branches remain inside one completed operator; no primewise branch norm is
introduced.

For the same `family.visiblePrimes` list selected by the arithmetic owner,
Mathlib's Banach-space interval fundamental theorem is applied to

```text
alpha |-> actualRootSandwichedSoninBand owner lambda alpha family.visiblePrimes.
```

Using the existing operator-norm derivative theorem and the endpoint identity
`actualRootSandwichedSoninBand_one_sub_zero`, Lean proves

```text
IntervalIntegrable
  (fun alpha => actualMovingSoninRootFlow owner lambda alpha
    family.visiblePrimes) volume 0 1
  ->
integral_0^1 actualMovingSoninRootFlow(alpha) d alpha
    = -rootSandwichedBandResponse owner lambda family.
```

The interval-integrability witness is deliberately explicit.  It is a
regularity obligation for the complete synchronized flow, not a hidden
positivity, trace, Gate 3U, or RH assumption.  A successor should discharge
that witness from continuity of the parameterized Euler/Gram flow, then bound
the integrated signed Sonin crossing while keeping the completed operator
recombined.

For every vector `u` in the actual finite-S common-log carrier, the module
applies the continuous linear coefficient map

```text
T |-> <u,T u>
```

to Proof 446's Bochner operator integral.  Lean proves

```text
integral_0^1 <u,actualMovingSoninRootFlow(alpha)u> d alpha
  = -<u,rootSandwichedBandResponse u>.
```

At every legal synchronized time, Proof 445's complete-crossing identity and
adjoint symmetry give the pointwise real density

```text
Re <u,actualMovingSoninRootFlow(alpha)u>
  = -2 Re <u,actualCompletedRootCrossing(alpha)u>.
```

This equality preserves the complete five-branch physical crossing after the
radial branch is deleted.  No branchwise absolute value or primewise norm is
introduced.

For any Hilbert basis and any finite index set `J`, the module then proves

```text
sum_(i in J) Re <basis_i,rootSandwichedBandResponse basis_i>
  = -integral_0^1
      sum_(i in J) Re <basis_i,actualMovingSoninRootFlow(alpha)basis_i>
    d alpha.
```

Only `intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum` is used to exchange the finite sum
and the integral.  This is a finite diagonal truncation of the real
infinite-dimensional operator, not a finite-matrix model.  It does not justify
an infinite `tsum`/integral exchange.  The next analytic producer must give
uniform summable-diagonal or trace-norm control, preserve the signed complete
crossing, and then pass to the ordinary trace.  Proof 430's coherent synthesis
guard remains active: diagonal Euler energy alone cannot supply that control.

The generic theorem

```text
ordinaryTraceAlong_re_abs_le_of_finiteDiagonalIntegralBound
```

starts with two inputs on the actual finite-S carrier and one named Hilbert
basis:

```text
IsTraceClassAlong basis rootSandwichedBandResponse

forall finite J,
  abs integral_0^1
    sum_(i in J) Re <basis_i,actualMovingSoninRootFlow(alpha)basis_i>
  d alpha
  <= C.
```

Proof 447 turns the second input into the same bound for every finite endpoint
diagonal sum.  The first input makes the real diagonal summable.  Lean then
uses `Summable.hasSum`, whose directed net is indexed by all finite subsets,
composes that net with the continuous absolute-value function, and passes the
closed inequality to the limit.  The conclusion is

```text
abs Re ordinaryTraceAlong(basis,rootSandwichedBandResponse) <= C.
```

This argument does not form

```text
integral_0^1 tsum_i density(alpha,i) d alpha
```

and therefore needs neither a `tsum`/integral exchange nor an absolutely
summable time-density majorant.  It also does not take branchwise trace norms.
This is the correct signed limiting route around the total-variation guards
from Proofs 260 and 430.

The canonical theorem

```text
canonicalOrdinaryTraceAlong_re_abs_le_supportRadiusPolynomial_of_finiteDiagonalBound
```

uses the exact `canonicalFamily owner` and specializes `C` to

```text
2 * (owner.supportRadius + log 3)
  * (1 + owner.supportRadius + log 3).
```

It is now enough to prove this same bound for every finite canonical diagonal
signed integral and construct the actual same-carrier endpoint trace-class
witness.  The source-carrier theorem
`sourceBandGramResponse_isTraceClassAlong` is not silently reused: it concerns
a different carrier and does not by itself instantiate the global
`rootSandwichedBandResponse` premise.  Compactness and finite sections also do
not imply that premise.

The route audit found that Proof 450's hypothesis

```text
forall finite J, abs(sum_(i in J) a_i)<=C
```

must not be treated as the only analytic route.

converge to the ordinary diagonal `tsum`.  Proof 447 converts each prefix to
the corresponding signed moving-flow integral.  Endpoint self-adjointness

Finite matrix trace cyclicity legally cancels only the first line, leaving

```text
Tr(M_N(A B-B A))
```

object to estimate uniformly in `N`.

The total representative `actualCompletedRootCrossingOnUnit` uses the
genuine crossing for `|alpha|<=1` and zero outside.  On the actual integration
interval Lean proves

```text

  = 2 * integral_0^1 Re Tr(C_N(alpha)) d alpha.
```

The Hermitian factor `2` is restored algebraically in the conclusion.  No

Proof 491 audits the previously unused
`sourceCorrectedPhysicalSourcePairData`.  The generic ring lemma in
`CCM24FiniteSCorrectedPhysicalPairAlignment.lean` proves that an idempotent
outer support collapses the identity-transport corrected bracket to its
compressed signed ledger.  On the actual carriers, with `T` the complete
CC20 three-branch commutator,

```text
correctedPhysicalBracket(E,...,I)=E T E.
```

```text
C_S=J^dagger T E H_S J G_S^-1.
```

forward support causality, and never use `sourceCorrectedPhysicalSourcePairData`
alone as the Gate 3U estimator.  Proof 490's complete paired gauge owner is
the active object; compact root support must be used before its first absolute
value.  The family-uniform bound, Gate 3U, the finite-S sign, negative-owner
integration, Burnol's identity, and RH remain open.

2026-07-22 Proof 492 replaces the old three-coordinate source-remainder
legality pair by a common-left physical pair which retains the only available
raw endpoint cancellation through the first Hilbert--Schmidt energy.  Put

```text
T=L^dagger M=cc20ThreeBranchCommutator,
J=sourceInclusion,
V_S=B A_S J,
C_S=H_S J G_S^-1=finiteEulerMetricCoframe.
```

The new generic `boundedPrecompAddRight` constructor combines two bounded
precompositions with the same left map by adding their right legs.  Its actual
finite-S specialization proves

```text
raw remainder=J^dagger T(V_S+C_S)-V_S^dagger T J.
```

The corresponding pair is

```text
left =(LJ,LV_S),
right=(M(V_S+C_S),-MJ).
```

Thus the forward first jet and raw endpoint contribute the single energy
`norm(M(V_S+C_S))^2`, not the orthogonal sum
`norm(MV_S)^2+norm(MC_S)^2`.  Lean proves that its trace product is exactly
`sourceActualBandFiniteEulerRemainderResponse` and exactly Proof 490's
`lowerFactorGaugedActualBandCompletedRelativeResponse`.  Fixed-family trace
legality follows from the explicit pair itself.

This does not prove Gate 3U.  No contraction or family-uniform operator-norm
bound for `V_S+C_S` is asserted.  The active analytic target is now the
source-specific column estimate

```text
sum_i norm(M((V_S+C_S)e_i))^2
  <=support--Sobolev polynomial independent of S,
```

with the complete physical leg and compact root support retained.  Splitting
that column back into `MV_S` and `MC_S` recreates the inverse lower-factor
loss.  The finite-S sign, negative-owner integration, Burnol's identity, and
RH remain open.

2026-07-22 Proof 493 implements the combined-coframe biorthogonal guard
promised after Proof 492.  The new source module is
`ConnesWeilRH/Source/CCM25Concrete/CCM24FiniteSCombinedCoframeGuard.lean`,
with focused audit
`ConnesWeilRH/Dev/CCM24FiniteSCombinedCoframeGuardAudit.lean` and proof note
`docs/proofs/493_combined_coframe_biorthogonal_guard.md`.

The exact source objects are

```text
J   = sourceInclusion
R   = sourceSoninProjection
V_S = sourceActualBandForwardCoframe
C_S = finiteEulerMetricCoframe
D_S = V_S + C_S
L_S = (I-R) D_S
```

The Lean ledger now proves, on the literal source Sonin carrier,

```text
R V_S = 0,
J^dagger V_S = 0,
J^dagger D_S = I,
R D_S = J,
D_S = J + L_S,
L_S = V_S + sourceSoninCoframeLeakage,
J^dagger L_S = 0,
R L_S = 0.
```

The first zero is source-specific: `R B=0` for the actual quotient band
`B`, rather than an abstract frame assumption.  The two biorthogonal
identities for `C_S` come from the existing Gram-corrected metric coframe
ledger.  The final pair theorem rewrites the first right leg of Proof 492 as

```text
M(D_S u) = M((J+L_S)u)
```

while deliberately not distributing `M` over the sum.  This preserves the
only available physical cancellation before Hilbert--Schmidt energy is
formed.

The guard closes a carrier/alignment gap only.  Biorthogonality fixes the
`J^dagger` component and says nothing about the size of the off-Sonin column:
the elementary shear `J x=(x,0)`, `D_A x=(x,A x)` has `J^dagger D_A=I` while
its L2 norm grows with `A`.  Therefore no Julia contraction, operator-norm
bound, Gate 3U estimate, finite-S sign, negative-owner integration, Burnol
identity, or RH conclusion may be attached to Proof 493.

2026-07-22 Proof 496 completes the revised three-step producer batch without
promoting it to Gate 3U.  Step 1 is the actual suffix Schur--polar telescope
in `CCM24FiniteSSchurPolarTelescoping.lean`; its terminal Julia survivor is
exactly the adjoint of the complete ordered source transition.  Step 3 is the
family-independent source input in `CCM24FiniteSFixedPhysicalSourceInput.lean`:
the positive Gram square root of the complete fixed source physical pair has
basis energy at most twice `fixedPhysicalEnergyMajorant`.

The originally proposed Step 2, a single positive right-leg readout of the
combined coframe, is false.  At zero detector it would force an unsupported
vanishing relation for the forward and metric coframes.  The replacement is
the actual forward/reverse Schur--Markov pair in
`CCM24FiniteSSchurMarkovPairing.lean`.  For each adjacent suffix Lean builds

```text
G_(p,S)=oldFrame^dagger normalizedForward_p newFrame,
R_(p,S)=newFrame^dagger normalizedInverse_p oldFrame
```

and proves

```text
G_(p,S) R_(p,S)=R_(p,S) G_(p,S)=rho_p I,
norm(G_(p,S))<=1,
norm(R_(p,S))<=1.
```

The chronological complete products satisfy

```text
Gamma_S Lambda_S=Lambda_S Gamma_S=rho_S I,
norm(Lambda_S)<=1,
rho_S=finiteEulerLowerFactor(S)/finiteEulerUpperFactor(S)>0.
```

The local selected-detector relative numerator is proved directly on the
rectangular carriers.  It is the complete moving-polar-boundary defect followed
by the reverse Markov transition; the older generic same-ring theorem cannot
be instantiated with rectangular frames.  The complete numerator is

```text
N_S=Gamma_S alpha_empty Lambda_S-rho_S alpha_S
```

and Lean proves the signed recursion

```text
N_(p::S)
 =G_(p,S) N_S R_(p,S)
  +N_(p,S)^local rho_S.
```

Thus the complete detector response is one finite signed cocycle.  No inverse
transition, inverse Gram norm, or primewise absolute value is introduced.

`CCM24FiniteSSchurMarkovCompletedReadout.lean` connects that cocycle to the
existing lower-factor-gauged completed response without an illegal trace
cycle.  The polar numerator and the route-ordered Gram endpoint have different
operator order, so the module retains the exact scaled ordering defect

```text
Delta_S^ord=N_S-rho_S sourceBandGramResponse_S.
```

With the complete actual first jet kept whole, Lean proves the unconditional
same-object identity

```text

 :=rho_S actualBandFirstJet_S-N_S+Delta_S^ord
 =rho_S lowerFactorGaugedActualBandCompletedRelativeResponse_S.
```

The ordinary-trace scaling follows from this operator equality under the
already existing fixed-family trace-legality witness.  It does not cyclically
permute a positive similarity.  The first jet and ordered endpoint retain the
outer, reflected-outer, second-support, and prolate branches before any trace

```text
 <=rho_S C (1+B_root)^d norm(g)_(H^r)^2
```

with constants independent of the finite visible-prime family.  The revised
