at the ordinary-trace level.  The result is good as an exact reduction, but it
does not close Gate 3U.  The new module
`CCM24FiniteSSchurMarkovPolarTraceBridge.lean` constructs the terminal polar

```text
R_S=Gamma_S^(-1/2),
L_S=Gamma_S^(-1/2) Gamma_S
```

and proves both `R_S L_S=I` and `L_S R_S=I`.  The full forward and reverse
polar similarities include the fixed empty-suffix coordinate on opposite
sides.  Lean only uses the available square identity

```text
Z_empty Z_empty=I.
```

It does not assume the stronger unproved statement `Z_empty=I`; the two empty
coordinates cancel inside the assembled forward/base/reverse detector
product.

The complete transition products are identified exactly as

```text
transitionProduct_S=upper_S^(-1) F_S,
reverseProduct_S=lower_S R_S^complete,
rho_S=lower_S/upper_S.
```

Combining these identities with Proof 496's ordered numerator gives

```text
N_S
 =rho_S L_S leftOrderedSourceBandGramResponse_S R_S.
```

No primewise absolute value or inverse transition is introduced.  The
similarity is not removed by a formal infinite-dimensional trace cycle.
Instead, `ordinaryTraceAlong_polarLeftSimilarity_eq_leftOrdered` sandwiches
the existing swapped four-branch Hilbert--Schmidt pair and performs two legal
pair trace cycles.  Because the left- and right-Gram responses are adjoints,
the final theorems are

```text
Tr(N_S)=rho_S conjugate(Tr(sourceBandGramResponse_S)),
abs Tr(N_S)=rho_S abs Tr(sourceBandGramResponse_S).
```

The conjugation is retained at the complex trace level; the two operator
orders are never identified.  The exact remaining Gate 3U producer is

```text
abs Tr(N_S)
 <=rho_S C (1+B_root)^d norm(g)_(H^r)^2
```

with constants independent of the visible finite-prime family and the whole

this estimate is exactly equivalent to the corresponding route endpoint
bound; it supplies no estimate itself.  Gate 3U, the finite-S sign,

`CCM24FiniteSActualSchurGraphSupportDefect.lean`.  It names the exact ambient
graph-support defect

and proves the arbitrary-cosine Euler action, the projected graph-frame
transport identity, and the left-inverse readback.  The actual identities are

Proof 553's four-term ledger has the exact residual normal form

```text
R_(p,S) = Phi(Delta_S) T_(p,S)^dagger

Phi(Delta) = J^dagger K Delta - Delta^dagger K J.
```

Proof 554 then gives the ambient one-prime obstruction to estimating that
residual independently through Proof 506's antiresonant loss.  For
`a=p^(-1/2)`, the physical inverse and normalized Schur transport have

```text
p(z) = (1-a)/(1-a z),
t(z) = (1-a z)/(1+a),
(p-t)(-1) = -2a/(1+a) != 0,
```

while the loss square root has symbol `sqrt(a)/(1+a) * (1+z)` and vanishes
at `z=-1`.  Fourier wave packets near `-1` therefore make the ratio of the
physical transport difference to the ambient loss arbitrarily large.  This
strictly rejects a residual-only Douglas producer on the ambient
translation-invariant carrier; it does not reject a full-row cancellation
after source frames, projections, and the moving-boundary channel are
recombined.  The live target remains the combined signed raw row, Gate 3U,
the finite-S sign, Burnol's identity, and RH remain open.

2026-07-25 Proof 560 adds
`CCM24FiniteSCompletedJuliaCanonicalAnalysisBridge.lean` and its focused audit.
The foundational `CCM24FiniteSDouglasFactor.lean` now also proves the exact
range-supported Douglas construction
`exists_range_supported_factor_of_norm_eq`. If bounded maps `A` and `B` have

```text
||A x|| = ||B x||
```

for every source vector, the constructed factor `F` satisfies

```text
||F|| <= 1,
F * B = A,
F† * F * B = B.
```

The last identity is not available from an arbitrary witness returned by
`exists_factor_of_norm_le`: such a witness can have a component on the
orthogonal complement of `range B`. Proof 560 uses the extension on
`closure (range B)` followed by the orthogonal projection onto that closure,
then extends the norm identity from the dense range by continuity.

On the actual CCM24 finite-S carriers, let `L` be the adjacent Julia
`leftCoDefect`, `A` the packed ambient-plus-moving-boundary analysis, and `F`
the canonical factor. The new bridge proves same-bound conversions:

```text
raw = L * R
  ->  (R† * F†) * A = raw†,

D * A = raw†
  ->  raw = L * (D * F)†.
```

It also transports the conversion across every visible-prime/suffix pair and
proves the uniform nonempty-factor/readout equivalence. Operator order is kept
literal; no physical channel is split and no readout is obtained from an
arbitrary factor without the range-left-inverse identity.

`CCM24FiniteSCompletedJuliaResidualOnlyAntiresonantObstruction.lean`, its
focused audit, and `docs/proofs/561_residual_only_antiresonant_obstruction.md`.
It formalizes the exact antiresonant spectral-fibre guard used by Proof 554:

```text
U = -I,
E = I - (1/2) U = (3/2) I,
P = (1/2) E^-1 = (1/3) I,
T = (1 + 1/2)^-1 E = I,
```

is zero.  The formal theorem

operator `F` can satisfy `P - T = F Q`.  This is a spectral-fibre
no-go theorem only: it does not assert that the global `L2` carrier contains

factorization

```text
R_(p,S)^dagger (primeEulerAmbientLossFactor p)^dagger=C_(p,S).
```

bound. Lean consequently proves same-bound equivalence between the
route-uniform two-step-factor predicate and one route-uniform ambient-loss
factor predicate. The existential forms are also equivalent.

by `2B`. At horizon one this gives the scaled complete-target size bound
`2B`. Thus Proof 656's factor alone reaches the paired adjoint-coboundary
envelope, Proof 649's pointwise target, and the existing raw and renewed

factor route. The reverse implication remains invalid: a horizon-one size
bound does not construct the factor.

2026-07-30 Proof 670 isolates the quantitative gap between the restricted raw
Bone 1 estimate and Proof 648's full ambient-loss quotient. An initial route
audit rejected rebuilding a Weyl/approximate-kernel sequence: the existing
`CompactApproximateKernel` and completed-Julia obstruction modules already
prove qualitative target decay on bounded approximate kernels, but do not
compare decay rates or produce a Douglas bound.

For a route-valid `(p,S)`, write

```text
A_p=(primeEulerAmbientLossFactor p)^dagger,
F_S=newSuffixFrame unitSoninScale S,
I_(p,S)=signedCompressedInteriorOwner_(p,S),
C_(p,S)=I_(p,S)F_S^dagger.
```

The raw predicate with constant `B` is first converted from squared norms to

```text
||I_(p,S)x||<=B||A_pF_Sx||.
```

Proof 670 names route-uniform frame-loss stability with constant `K`:

```text
||A_pF_SF_S^dagger u||<=K||A_pu||.
```

The exact same-vector chain is then

```text
||C_(p,S)u||
  =||I_(p,S)F_S^dagger u||
  <=B||A_pF_SF_S^dagger u||
  <=B*K||A_pu||.
```

The existing Douglas theorem constructs
`SuffixCompleteCoupledAmbientLossFactorData` with norm bound `B*K` for every
route-valid step. Route quantification gives Proof 648's ambient-loss factor
gate, and Proof 669 converts it without further cost to the two-step factor
and paired finite-horizon envelope.

The module also formalizes the Hilbert countermodel

```text
H=WithLp 2 (Complex x Complex),
F x=(x,0),
F^dagger(x,z)=x,
A_epsilon(x,z)=(x+z,epsilon z),
C=F^dagger.
```

For `epsilon!=0`, `A_epsilon` is injective; `F^dagger F=I`; and the restricted
comparison is equality with constant one. For `u=(1,-1)`, however,

```text
||C u||=1,
||A_epsilon u||=epsilon,
||A_epsilon F F^dagger u||=1.
```

Thus both ambient domination and frame-loss stability force
`1<=K*epsilon`; choosing `epsilon=(K+1)^(-1)` proves that neither admits a
uniform `K` over the family. This only blocks a generic inference from
injectivity/isometric-frame structure. It is not a no-go theorem for the
actual real-line finite-S owner.

2026-07-30 Proof 671 identifies Proof 670's remaining frame-loss stability
with one concrete relative commutator estimate on the actual common-log
carrier. For a visible prime `p` and suffix `S`, write

```text
U_p=U_(log p),
Q_p=I+U_p,
s_p=primeEulerAmbientLossScale p,
P_S=newSuffixRangeProjection unitSoninScale S.
```

The existing ambient factorization and Gram-projection theorems give the
literal source identifications

```text
(primeEulerAmbientLossFactor p)^dagger=s_p Q_p,

P_S
  =parameterizedCanonicalGramProjection unitSoninScale 1 S
  =starProjection_(ccm24SemilocalSoninClosedSubspace unitSoninScale S).
```

The scale is positive and therefore cancels from the same-vector norm
comparison. The second identity makes `P_S` an actual orthogonal projection,
so `||P_Sv||<=||v||`. With the repository commutator convention
`[A,P]=AP-PA`, Lean proves

```text
[Q_p,P_S]=[U_p,P_S],

Q_pP_Su=[U_p,P_S]u+P_SQ_pu,

[U_p,P_S]u=Q_pP_Su-P_SQ_pu.
```

Consequently a route-uniform relative commutator bound `L`

```text
||[U_p,P_S]u||<=L||Q_pu||
```

gives frame-loss stability with constant `L+1`. Conversely, frame-loss
stability with constant `K` gives the relative commutator bound `K+1`.
Proof 671 packages this as an existential equivalence, not as a producer of
either bound.

The direct consumer chain is now

```text
restricted raw Bone 1 B
  + actual relative commutator L
  -> ambient-loss factor B*(L+1)
  -> Proof 669 two-step factor B*(L+1)
  -> paired finite-horizon envelope.
```

The ordinary estimate `||[U_p,P_S]u||<=2||u||` is unusable for this purpose.
The required right side is `||(I+U_p)u||`, which can decay on antiresonant
approximate-kernel vectors while `||u||` remains bounded. Any next producer
must retain the actual semilocal support, Fourier-support, and prolate
branches until their signed commutator cancellation is compared with the
same antiresonant denominator. Estimating those branches separately in
operator norm loses the needed information.

```text
E(E D - Q E D) + (E Q E D - R D) = E D - R D,
```

using radial idempotence on the already radial vector `E D u`.  This avoids
rewriting through the Sonin compression in the wrong syntactic shape and keeps
the statement as a pure algebraic channel recombination.

The endpoint contraction target is now equivalently

```text
sourceOuterCoframeLeakage
  + (sourceActualBandForwardCoframe + sourceBandMetricCoframeLeakage)
  = 0.
```

This is not a proof that either channel vanishes separately.  It does not
prove Gate 3U, the finite-S sign, Burnol's identity, or
`_root_.RiemannHypothesis`.  The next producer must keep the outer leakage
and the forward-plus-band metric leakage as one signed same-object equation
unless a new theorem proves a legal separation.

outer/reflected-second-support/prolate pairing before the first absolute
value. The scalar lower-factor gauge alone cannot create this gain because
the paired projection owner is exactly gauge invariant.
